Breads and Breakfasts 361
| OATMEAL SUGGESTIONS | SUGGESTIONS

Fresh from the stove top, oatmeal (or quinoa) is not only a healthy addi-
tion to your sports diet but also an easy-to-digest preexercise breakfast. If
cooking first thing in the morning is not your cup of tea, prepare cook-free
overnight oats the night before. Simply toss 1/2 cup (40 g) uncooked oats,
1 cup (240 ml) milk (or 2/3 cup [160 ml] milk and 1/3 cup [75 g] Greek
yogurt) into an empty peanut butter jar, add extras as desired (such as chia,
flax, maple syrup, salt), shake well, and let it sit in the refrigerator for at
least four hours or overnight. In the morning, you'll have a pudding-like
porridge you can grab for breakfast on the go.

The following oatmeal (or quinoa) suggestions will add variety to your
breakfasts.

¢ Dried apricot pieces, honey, and a dash of nutmeg

© Raisins, cinnamon, and slivered almonds

¢ Sliced banana (cooked with the oatmeal), brown sugar, and

peanut butter

¢ Dried cranberries, honey, and chopped pecans

¢ Diced apple (cooked with the oatmeal) or applesauce, walnut
